site.name: Newport Castle
site.description: A ruined castle in Newport, Wales. Built in the 14th century believed to be by Hugh de Audley, 1st Earl of Gloucester to manage the crossing of the River Usk and administer taxes.

osmTags.inscription: In memory of the allied invasion of Europe on 6th June 1944. This plaque was erected by the people of Newport on 6th June 1994 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the D-Day landings by the allied forces in Normandy during World War II.

The Murenger. John Frost was one of the owners of this building which dates from 1533. His draper's shop also stood on this side of High Street until the late 1870s. Once home to the High Sherilf of Monmouthshire, today The Murenger is a public house.

GRIGGS & VAUGHAN
ARCHITECTS
JOHN JENKINS LTD. CONTRACTORS
1926

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Location and terrain only. OpenStreetMap has no mapped outline for this site.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
